utterances.text: And so we thank you for your advocacy, and I heard you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: You are going to make sure

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Young people are treated right, and we are there too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: But as you said to them, this is a crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: I've got to remind people, this is a secure facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: This is not a group home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: This is not a summer camp.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: This is a secure facility that is charged with the protection of those who are confined to their facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: And having said that, my Vice President Robinson will go next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Derek Robinson, vice president of grievances and legal services for Local 371, says initiatives were announced without meaningful union engagement. He says members face overcrowding, staffing shortages, violence, and complex clinical needs, and that programs on paper need staffing, training, space, and security.
chapters.title: Local 371 VP Derek Robinson testifies on staffing and violence

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Stevens and members of the Committee on Children and Youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: My name is Derek Robinson, the Vice President of Grievances, Legal Services for SSEU Local 371.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: We represent our youth development specialists, program counselors, caseworkers, congregate care specialists, and frontline employees who do this work every day in detention, juvenile detention that is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: SSEU Local 371 is deeply concerned that these initiatives were publicly announced without meaningful engagement with the union regarding the operational impact on youth development specialists, caseworkers, program counselors as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Our members are not simply

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Observers of the juvenile justice system, they are the professionals responsible for carrying out these policies in real time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Inside facilities where overcrowding, staffing shortages,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Violence, security concerns, and increasingly complex behavior and clinical needs are daily realities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: The people making these announcements must understand that there are significant differences between announcing a plan and successfully implementing it inside a juvenile detention facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: One, programming must reflect the reality inside Crossroads and Horizon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: The young people detained at crossroads in Horizon Juvenile Centers individually facing allegations of extremely serious offenses, including murder, attempted murder, and other violent crimes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: These are circumstances that can involve significant security, behavioral and clinical considerations that must be addressed before programming can be implemented safely and effectively.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Members understand that rehabilitation and the public safety are not competing objectives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Both are essential, but a program on paper is only as effective as the staffing, training, supervisors, space security, and resources available to support it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Additional staffing must translate into actual substantial coverage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Recruitment and retention efforts, including strategies reduced turnover rate, appropriate training before employees are assigned to these demanding facilities,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: The resources necessary to protect both employees and the young adults.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: We need staffing plans that reflect the actual conditions inside these facilities, not simply the number of positions announced in a press release.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Ongoing violence require immediate intervention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: This is one of the most urgent concerns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: This is one of our most urgent concerns is the violence dealing in both of these facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Our position is straightforward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: There's a big disconnect between

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: The agency, the leadership of this agency, and our members is a big disconnection that they're not adhering to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: That's more extremely why we're dealing with

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: a crisis and they have no urgency of the way they're dealing with this crisis, no urgency whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Thank you for giving us the time to testify and we look forward to any questions and answers you may have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Cassandra Washington, a grievance representative and 20-year youth development specialist, describes unsafe conditions including violence, unsanitary spaces, and chronic overcrowding. She says staff face burnout and recommends protective gear and relocating older residents age 18 to 21 to a separate facility.
chapters.title: Cassandra Washington describes unsafe conditions and staff burnout

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: My name is Cassandra Washington, and I'm a grievance representative at the Social Service Employees Union Local 371.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: On behalf of the president, on behalf of President Anthony Wells, our officers, staff, and the entirety of this membership,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: I want to thank the chairs in the honorable Letha Stevens of the Committee of Children and Youth for extending this opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: SSEU Local 371 represents the Youth Development Specialist Title Series.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Having proudly served in this title for over 20 years, I know firsthand how critical and valuable this role is to juvenile facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Yet despite the tireless and unwavering efforts of these workers, severe systemic challenges continuously hinder their ability to safely and effectively support the youth in their care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: We are deeply concerned by the multitude unsafe conditions currently persisting within the Department of the Youth and Family Justice Facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: These issues directly threaten the safety, health, and well-being of both our staff members and the juveniles in custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: While juvenile facilities are mandated to provide a secure, structured, and rehabilitative environment, compromised safety creates unnecessary risks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: heightens stress, and undermines the system's core responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Right now, staff and youth are facing unacceptable dangers, including pervaded violence, unsanitary living spaces, and chronic overcrowding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: This is a critical threat that remains unresolved despite previous

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: previous engagements with agency leadership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: These hazards expose everyone in the facilities to physical injury, emotional distress, potential sexual assaults, and repeated psychological trauma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Vulnerable youths who are already struggling with behavior or emotional challenges are especially

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: damaged by these volatile environments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Co-currently, the inaction on these safety concerns leads to crippling stress, severe fatigue, and burnout among our staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: This crushing work land directly impacts employees'morale,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: critical decision-making, and daily job performance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Without adequate training, protective resources, and logistical support, staff face an uphill battle when responding to emergencies, conflicts, or behavior crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Ensuring staff safety is absolutely essential to ensuring staff safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: It's absolutely essential to the stability of the facility and the resources rehabilitation of the youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: These compassing crises can be, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Can be drastically reduced by immediately implementing two proven solutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: One, providing sufficient protective gear, which is issuing neck guards, cut-proof gloves, and protective sleeves to immediate...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Please wrap up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Please wrap up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: To immediately...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: mitigate sharp objects injury risk, relocating adult residents, aggressively restationing older residents age 18 to 21 to separate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: We suggest such as the Element Queen facility located in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Cassandra Washington
utterances.text: Facility administrators and agency leaders.

chapters.summary: Youth Development Specialist DeColby Hester gives a firsthand account of the June 21 Horizon riot. He describes weapons, keys taken from staff, overcrowded housing units with 22 residents each, a five-plus-hour riot, injuries at Lincoln Hospital, and NYPD being denied entry twice.
chapters.title: DeColby Hester gives firsthand account of June 21 Horizon riot

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: My name is DeColby Hester.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: Good evening, Chair Stevens and all others in attendance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: My name is Jacoby Hester.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I am a youth development specialist at Horizons Juvenile Detention Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I'm here to provide firsthand observations and information regarding workplace safety, staffing, security procedures, and the conditions under which youth development specialists are expected to perform their duties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I understand you just painted a beautiful picture, but let me tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: June 21st, 2026, at approximately 4.45 p.m., a serious disturbance occurred inside the facility involving residents attacking staff to the assigned housing units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: Based on the information and accounts available to staff, weapons involved in the incidents included surgical scalpels, shanks, screwdrivers, meat cleavers, and other improvised weapons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: Once fear was established by the youth, keys were forcibly removed from the staff's possessions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: Residents then vacated their assigned housing units and gained access to upper B quarters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: The situation...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: as residents from multiple housing units came into contact with one another.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: The housing units involved included units E, F, and G.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: Although these units are ordinarily designed to accommodate approximately 15 individuals, I understand that the housing units had 22 residents each.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: This raises concerns regarding overcrowding, supervision, and the ability to maintain safe operations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: During the disturbance, youth development specialists attempted to intervene and restore order using defensive tactics and restraint techniques available to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: The SCM tactics are antiquated and do not include weapons retrieval.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: YDS were rendered defenseless and made to observe youth and staff get sliced, punched, slammed, and even staff shanks having shanks held to their throats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: The riot continued for five plus hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I arrived later that evening as I was slated to work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: However, I came in my union capacity, my union delegate capacity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I was then directed by SSEU Local 371 Vice President Derek Robinson to report to Lincoln Hospital to document injuries sustained by employees during the incident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: Be it known that no member of executive management showed any care or concern or visited the hospital while I was there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: At hospital, I personally observed several employees receiving treatment for serious injuries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: These include deep lacerations, significant facial and head trauma injuries involving eye

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: sockets and other wounds consistent with the accounts of the violence inside the facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I also observed a colleague receiving anesthesia so that medical personnel could treat and reposition his injured arm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: These first-hand observations reinforce my concerns about the risk employees face when facility security and staff arrangements fail to provide adequate protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I also take reservation to NYPD.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: NYPD being denied entry not once but twice on that day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I thank you for your time and consideration, and I welcome all questions.

chapters.summary: Stevens asks the union about its meeting cadence with the new ACS commissioner. Anthony Wells says the union has met several times and welcomes town halls, but wants action and says the administration's plan was not shared with the union initially.
chapters.title: Stevens asks union about meeting cadence with ACS commissioner

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Thank you all for coming and testifying today and staying.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Just one question, because I know the commissioner has been doing these town halls.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Have you guys met with her?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: What does those regular cadence look like?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I know even the incident that you're talking about happened.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: That was like her fifth day on the job and has been.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: You know, running ever since.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: What is your cadence in meeting with the new commissioner?

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: What has that been like?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: So, first of all, we welcome the town halls.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We don't get involved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: That's her meeting with her staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We want the staff to be able to talk to her freely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: She has been willing to meet with us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We've met several times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: But like you observed earlier,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: It's time for action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They have this plan that they didn't share with us, by the way, when they first announced it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Didn't tell us anything about it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: And when they talk about stakeholders, you hear one of them say,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Anything about the union being a stakeholder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We believe that there's not a real commitment on the part of the local management to, one, correct these issues immediately that recognize there's a crisis that you said earlier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They're acting like this is like, okay, we got plans, we got programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We should be disputing something that they're talking about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Kids are sleeping on desks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: You got pictures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Kids are sleeping on the floor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: This is not made up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: And we have been advocating that the 18 to 21-year-olds be moved to a separate facility that will cut down on some of the overcrowded immediately.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We're not saying they're going to go under the DOC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They can stay under.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: D-Y-F-J.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: D-Y-F-J.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: So they could stay there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: But they need to be in a different facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: But there's no commitment to that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: It's a commitment to programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We're in favor of programs.

chapters.summary: Wells details union safety demands, including body cameras, returning keys to hall staff, and protective gear. He says there is a severe staff shortage and questions where the policy and accountability are when policies are violated.
chapters.title: Union details safety demands: body cams, keys, and protective gear

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We said, let's bring in body cams.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: No further discussion about body cams.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We asked for body cams.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They had a policy where...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They took the keys away from the workers on the hall and had a person assigned in the hallway with the keys.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: One, you have a staff shortage, a severe staff shortage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Two, you're asking this person in the hall.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: You believe that there's currently a staff shortage?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: It's a staff shortage for two reasons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: One, because some people...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Find that this is not their job, but people are getting hurt and they're staying out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: And so there's a staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: So we asked for a budget that had counted earlier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We talked about they make plans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They said they created uniforms to escort kids to school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: That's a YDS job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: When did you make that decision that you were going to do this?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: What was the discussion with this union, okay, to do this?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: So we don't see that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: The commissioner just got here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: And we've met three or four times already.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: But as I told her when we met last time, we're not going to just meet to meet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We're not just going to meet to have you talk about programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: What should they do?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Listen, I've been advocating.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Are you guys, when you're meeting, are you guys coming with suggestions?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Well, we have suggestions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: We have done suggestions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Some of their stuff is our suggestions.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So they are taking your feedback and some of it.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Well, in the long run.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And that's not a bad thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: In the long run, some of the stuff, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: But in the short term, the protective gear, they're giving the keys back to the people on the dome.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: That unilocks everybody in this title because we need all hands on deck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Where's the policy?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: What happens when policies are violated?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Who's held responsible?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: There's no policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Okay, since June 21st, which was a major riot, where they did refuse to let the police in, it took hours to get control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Where's the policy that says,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: It's very simple, sister.

chapters.summary: Wells and Stevens discuss the NYPD response, persistent contraband, and the broader crisis. Wells says when a facility is out of control, outside help is needed; Robinson says there are no consequences and alleges pizza parties rewarded youth after the riot.
chapters.title: Union and Chair discuss NYPD response and contraband

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: By the way, I just want to be on record.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I agree not letting it in my PD because I might have escalated, but I hear your concern as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: No, no, but, but, but, but, but.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: When a place is out of control and people are getting hurt, both residents and children, you got to do something different.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: You cannot allow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: I'm not, listen, I'm not against, but a situation where there's nobody getting control, you need help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: And you can have control help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: You can't say, oh, well, and it was downplayed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: But meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: This delegate, this vice president was out there, went to the hospital, people got hurt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They're still, the security is not consistent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: People have been observed not going through their security.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Contraband.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: This union is against, I can't say enough times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Contraband puts everybody at risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They're still in contravention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They're people still, they still have scalpels, okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They're getting it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: When this rise was happening, a mother went on TV and said, I speak to my kid every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: How does that happen?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Nobody has everyday telephone privilege.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: How is that happening?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: What's the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: Did anybody investigate what this mother was talking about?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They say, how is this happening?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: They still have pictures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: So my point is what you said earlier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: This is a crisis, and you have to address the crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: And I don't think the crisis is being addressed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: There's nothing that says...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Wells
utterances.text: This Christ is being dressed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: On the same page.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: And also, there's no consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: It's almost like...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: The agency is rewarding bad behavior because there's no way that you can have juveniles part of a major riot or gang assaults,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: attempted murder in the place, and then less than 24 hours later, they are having pizza parties for the individuals that were cutting and slicing and stabbing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Other youth as well as the staff that work at those facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Stuff like that, you just cannot have, you cannot have a deputy commissioner throw pizza parties and reward kids when they do bad things on these halls like that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: That's unacceptable.

chapters.summary: Stevens says she agrees consequences are needed but that pizza parties after assaults are unacceptable. She thanks the union panel and says she will continue fighting until young people are released and real solutions are in place.
chapters.title: Stevens agrees consequences needed but rejects pizza parties

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: No, I mean, that is unacceptable, and I'm never going to support that.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: But, you know, I think we also need to think about what those consequences are because, again, these are young people.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: But I don't think if you are assaulting people, you should be given pizza parties.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: That is unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: In the spirit of time and having to get to a couple of other panels, I want to say thank you, guys.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I want us to continue these conversations because this is not going to be the last conversation because, again, I am not shutting my mouth until these young people are released and we have real solutions moving forward.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So thank you guys for your time and being with us today.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Derek Robinson
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Bronx Borough President Vanessa Gibson joins by Zoom and thanks Chair Stevens for the hearing. She says she has visited Horizon, was horrified by conditions, and agrees the city is in a crisis that demands a crisis response.
chapters.title: Bronx Borough President Vanessa Gibson testifies on Horizon conditions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We will now be hearing from Vanessa Gibson, the Bronx Borough President, on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Am I here?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Hold on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - DeColby Hester
utterances.text: We can hear you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: You can hear me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I really appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And thank you, Chair Althea Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: You have been overseeing an incredible and a very productive hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: So I want to acknowledge you and the team at the City Council and the Committee on Children and Youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you very, very much for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I had a chance to watch it for the last hour.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: So I did hear Bronx District Attorney Darcelle Clark and her team.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I also heard the ACS commissioner and the administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I got to listen to a lot of your questions as well as your colleagues'questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: So let me just say as your Bronx Borough President, I am all in on the continued discussions around our city's juvenile justice system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Like you, Councilmember, I've had an opportunity to visit Horizon more than once and am horrified by the conditions of what I saw and everything you saw, I saw as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: So I know there's a lot of work that absolutely must be done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And I agree with you that this is a crisis and it demands a crisis response.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Just like we are in an urgency around affordability in this city, we absolutely need to be in a moment of urgency for the children that are in our juvenile justice system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: So I want to acknowledge you and thank you for today's important hearing to discuss how we improve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: the conditions for many of our justice-involved young people across the city of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Too many of our young people have become involved in the justice system, and it's a crisis, and we must do more to get them back on the right and stable track.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: We all have a collective obligation as elected officials, as city officials, advocates, families, and those affected to keep our schools and our communities free

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: from any sort of harm that would be imposed on our young people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: We have an obligation to do more, to show up differently for young people, as you always say.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And if we're not showing up for young people, then what are we doing, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair, again, because we understand that when our judicial system determines that detention is the optimal solution for a young person,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: we have to ensure that the conditions of that location, that detention facility, are conducive to rehabilitation so that they exit better than the way that they entered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Education and restorative justice programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Our city is not currently meeting that standard today, which means that more must happen.

chapters.summary: Gibson describes the June Father's Day weekend violence at Horizon and the facility's maintenance, space, cleanliness, overcrowding, staffing, and violence issues. She says she saw youth sleeping in classrooms on cots and calls for faster court processes, ATI/ATD expansion, non-secure detention, ICM, and restored Probation programs.
chapters.title: Gibson details Horizon problems and calls for interventions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: As you all know and have heard in June of this year, I believe it was Father's Day weekend, we saw a violent incident in Horizon Juvenile Center, which is in the Bronx, where over a dozen people were injured.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And I want to acknowledge the uniformed staff, the civilian staff at Horizon, and everyone that is

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: entrusted to care for the young people that are there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: This must be a renewed focus on the policies, the procedures, the guidelines, and the conditions that led to this incident, as well as ones that happened prior, as well as after.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Frankly, Horizon and Crossroad, I'm adding that as well, is not where it needs to be today for young people, their families, and the communities that they will be returning to after their sentence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Horizon is suffering with maintenance issues, space issues, capacity, cleanliness, overcrowding, staffing shortages, violence among crews, and many other violations that prevent successful outcomes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: When we have young people sleeping in classrooms, and yes, Chair Stevens, I saw that too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: That was the first thing I wanted to see when I got to Horizon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Show me the classroom spaces where our students are sleeping on cots.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I have not seen a picture of anyone sleeping on the floor, so make sure that you can share that with me as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: But clearly something has gone wrong over this process, over this time, and we need greater interventions to improve the conditions in Horizon and get the overcrowding and capacity issue under control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Speeding up the court process to ensure that no young person or persons are waiting for detention for their trial, considering and pursuing additional alternatives, ATI,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: ATD programs that many of you have talked about, non-secure detention, and intensive case monitoring.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: We also took...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: about that too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And restoring a lot of the programs at DOP, Department of Probation, that were cut, programs that we were definitely supportive of in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Expanding engagements with at-risk youth and their advocates, talking to families, building true

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: commodity and a continuum of care to prevent criminal justice involvement in the first place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And that includes everyone you talked about, Chair, not just probation, ACS, New York City Public Schools, DYCD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: It includes all of us, all of our crisis management system, partners that are working in our boroughs, in the city, everyone, the unions, the stakeholders, DC 37, Local 371, everyone must be a part of these conversations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And we have to make sure we invest in upgrades.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: When I was at Horizon, I said to the commissioner, why can these students not give this place a paint job?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: They need serious improvements at Horizon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And the talented students, we should make sure that they can be a part of that as well, making sure that the program is sufficient to meet the needs of the young people today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I had an opportunity when I was their chair, I talked to a lot of the young men.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I talked about their history of how they got there, why they're there, and how they need to be different when they leave.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I reminded them that their circumstance never defines who they are, but they can not only overcome, but they can get rehabilitated, they can be transformed, and they can exit much better than they

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: the way they entered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: We have a lot of work to do, Councilmember, but I understand and know the work ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I know the risks, but the ultimate goal is to break the cycle of the criminal justice system and recidivism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: So many young people getting rearrested, changing their neighborhoods, their environments, and where they're returning to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: That includes the school partners, the youth partners, and everyone else that is entrusted with the care of our young people and making sure that we invest in the infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Chair Stevens, you have been incredible on this issue over not just your time as council member, but prior to that as well.

chapters.summary: Gibson announces $3 million for Bronx Restore and funding for Project RISE, totaling $6 million over two years across several Bronx precincts. She calls for supporting staff and applying the West Bronx Community Safety Coalition model to juvenile justice.
chapters.title: Gibson announces Bronx Restore and Project RISE funding

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And I want to acknowledge Councilmember Pietina Sanchez mentioned it, and it's worth repeating as I close.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: We've been able to work with Governor Kathy Hochul and DCJS, the New York State Department Division of Criminal Justice Services that oversees a lot of the criminal justice work in the state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And we got $3 million for the Bronx Restore program over a two-year contract that was led with D.A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Clark, with Councilmember Sanchez, as well as Project RISE, Respond, Invest, Sustain, and Empower.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And total, these two programs, two years, $6 million, spanning over the 4-0 precinct, the 4-6, and the 5-2, the South Bronx and the West Bronx, parts of your district in District 16.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: We really have to do more to support the staff as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: And I know the YDS staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: the uniformed civilian staff, the healthcare professionals, the mental health workers,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Everyone is a part of this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I am committed, Chair Stevens, as you know, anything I can do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: We started the West Bronx Community Safety Coalition on the west side of the borough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: We should take that and apply it to the juvenile justice system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Because one thing I will say is it is a plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: That we are implementing and executing and it's working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: When you look at a lot of the partners we've included in our- Thank you, Borough President.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I was wrapping up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: I appreciate your time today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vanessa L. Gibson
utterances.text: Thanks so much.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I have to be strict and try to enforce the time because if not, I know we still have five more panels.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: For the next panel, we will be calling up Elle Tatum, David Moss, Nikesha Francis, Amanda McCarthy, and Dominique McNally.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: And while this panel is coming up, I want to just say shout out to the Bronx for showing up.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Our Bronx DA and her staff is still here.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Our borough president showing up.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: I want to just highlight we are taking this serious and want to make sure that we are being acknowledged for all working together and being a part of this because we really want to see changes happen.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: So thank you to our borough president and our DA.

chapters.summary: Laquisha Tatum testifies about her son's experiences at Horizon. She says he was attacked by staff, a later incident left him with 46 stitches and staples, and she has received little response from investigative agencies; she asks what accountability exists for staff abuse.
chapters.title: Parent Laquisha Tatum testifies about son attacked and cut at Horizon

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I am Laquisha Tatum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I am speaking on behalf of my son that actually was in custody at Horizons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: He had two situations during the time that he was there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Last year, I reached out to the Justice Department stating that my son was attacked by staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: The case was unfortunately unfounded.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I don't know what evidence that was used to have them to make that claim.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: But if they would have went back into my son's record, they would have saw that the pictures was taken.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: There was no way that my son fell.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: He was attacked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: He stated that there were staff standing outside the door.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Making sure that everyone was, you know, on P's and Q's so that the staff that attacked my son was not seen or no one was able to bust in that room while he bust my son's lip.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: He was, his lip was bust on the top and the bottom and the report stated that he fell.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: We all know that that's not what happened.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I would like to know, being that these children are being held accountable for their actions, what happened to staff and what actions are being held accountable towards them with the abuse that they are doing?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: This is...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: It's not something that's new.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: It seemed like it's getting pushed under the rug because I have reached out to multiple people and not one have contacted me yet and said, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Tatum, I'm here to help you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I heard what happened to your son.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Moving forward, this year he was in there for ankle monitor violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: We still don't have no concrete evidence on neither one of his cases, so I don't understand why the case is still going on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: As long as it is, it's about to be two years that these cases have been standing, and I have to get a paid lawyer for these cases to understand what's going on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: May 10th this year on Mother's Day, to be exact, my son was cut severely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: He was in the hospital, Harlem Hospital, for five days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Five days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: The situation happened at around 10 o'clock that night.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I didn't get a call until about 4 o'clock in the morning saying that they needed my consent to sedate my son in order for them to perform the proper

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: procedures that they needed in order for him to have his hand stitched up because between both hands he had 46 stitches and in the back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: On his back, he received three different cuts, and he had to get staples.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I reached out to 50 million people in the Justice Department.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I gave them my claim number.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: No one is reaching out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I reached out to the Department of Investigations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: No one still is telling me what's the status on these situations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: The only one who actually took the time out to reach out to me was Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Appreciate her for that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I would like to know what happened in these situations, understanding that they told me that there was a shortage in staff or whatever.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: That's the reason why they weren't able to assist my son when he got attacked and got cut by his peers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: He almost bled out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: He was in fainting stages because they lacked proper medical attention before they was able to call 911 to see that they honestly and obviously couldn't stop the bleeding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Yeah, so that was very disturbing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: And I understand that these kids are not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: All innocent, but again, they are human and they do have rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: I've seen dolls get treated better than them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: So yeah, it's just disturbing and disgusting that people even want to sit up here and try to take away their rights as humans and understand the logistics of everything that's going on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Not every child in there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laquisha Tatum
utterances.text: Is being held for something that they did and I know that firsthand.

utterances.speaker: Althea V. Stevens
utterances.text: Well, they're still children, but thank you for sharing with us today.

chapters.summary: Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy of CASES says the city continues to detain hundreds in horrific conditions without expanding alternatives. She cites declining Probation adjustment eligibility and an ACES success story, and urges support for Intro 447 and Reso 274.
chapters.title: Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy urges alternatives and Intro 447/Reso 274

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: I'm Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy, Senior Director and Youth Policy Lead at Cases.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Young New Yorkers need supportive programming in the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Instead, the city has continued to detain hundreds of young people in horrific conditions without expanding access to alternatives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Over the last several years, the Department of Probation has failed to identify young people eligible for adjustment, a process that connects them to a personalized plan for success.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Just 15% of young people overall were found eligible in 2026 compared to 61% in 2022.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Probation did not find a single high-risk young person eligible in the past three years, a precipitous drop from 11% in 2018.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: This decline reflects just one way that the department is failing young people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Effective program models like ACES, a multi-year anti-violence program for young men vulnerable to arrest, prove that voluntary services decrease community violence without requiring participation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Devin connected with ACES in 2022 but later disengaged.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: ACES staff continued to contact him during this period, but unfortunately Devin was incarcerated in 2024.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Upon release, Devin immediately reconnected with ACES and the team connected him with our GED program, provided mentoring and referrals to substance use and mental health services while helping him meet his probation requirements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: He grew confident and was ready to pursue his goals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Today, he has successfully earned his GED, enrolled in community college, and has moved into his own apartment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Progress for young people is nonlinear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Our clients'stories include serious challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: But their success shows that the city can make meaningful change by robustly expanding access to these programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: The city can do more by supporting Intro 447 and Resolution 274.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: We urge the council to move quickly to adopt 247 prior to the legislative session so that our city does not go another year without access to this critical funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Every young person deserves access to appropriate support and opportunities for growth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: New York City must act urgently to expand and build meaningful opportunities for young people to thrive and resolve their involvement in the criminal legal system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amanda Stegnero-McCarthy
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Dominique McNally of the Queens Community Justice Center supports Intros 447 and 629 and Reso 274. She says information alone is insufficient, capacity for complex youth must expand, and Intro 629 needs safeguards including legal counsel, clinical expertise, and confidentiality protections.
chapters.title: Dominique McNally supports Intros 447/629 and Reso 274 with safeguards

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Stevens and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: My name is Dominique McNally, and I serve as the clinical manager and Atlas Functional Family Therapy Program Director at Center for Justice Innovations, Queens Community Justice Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: The overcrowding and unsafe conditions in New York City's youth detention facilities are deeply concerning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: The city must ensure that young people have access to safe living conditions, consistent education, mental health care, and meaningful programming, including vocational training and reentry supports for emerging adults.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: However, addressing these concerns must go hand in hand with reducing the number of young people held in detention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: We support intro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: We support Intro 0447, which would improve awareness of available diversion programs and alternative to detention and incarceration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: However, information alone is insufficient.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: The city must also expand program capacity, particularly for young people with complex needs and serious charges, so that detention is not the default when appropriate alternatives are unavailable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: We also support Resolution 274, calling for New York City's inclusion in state Raise the Age funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: As Raise the Age has increased demand for community-based alternatives, providers need additional resources to deliver the individualized services young people require.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: Finally,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: We support the goals of Intro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: Join on our experience with pre-trial jail population review at Rikers Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: We believe individualized detention reviews could help identify young people who can safely return to their communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: However, several safeguards are essential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: Reviews must include each young person's own legal counsel rather than relying solely on institutional defense providers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: We also have concerns about ACS, coordinating release efforts given its responsibility for detention and about protecting sensitive information shared among agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: Review teams must include appropriate community-based and clinical expertise with strong confidentiality protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: Ultimately, improving conditions, expanding alternatives, and ensuring meaningful opportunities for release are all essential to reducing youth incarceration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dominique McNally
utterances.text: Thank you again for the opportunity to testify.

chapters.summary: Nikisha Francis of Good Shepherd Services describes the March 2026 youth justice convening and May report. She calls for trauma-informed services, reentry planning, $50 million for youth justice innovation, and restoration of DOP programs like Next Steps and Works Plus.
chapters.title: Nikisha Francis urges youth justice funding and DOP program restoration

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Stevens and the members of the Committee on Children and Youth for this oversight hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: My name is Nikisha Francis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: I am the Policy and Advocacy Manager at Good Shepherd Services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Good Shepherd Services operates foster care, prevention, juvenile justice, parent support, alternative to detention, summarizing Saturday Night Lights, the Summer Youth Employment Program,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: after school, care violence, cornerstone, beacon, and runaway and homeless youth program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: My testimony will focus on the information regarding alternatives to incarceration and alternatives to detention programs for youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: On March 6, 2026, this year, the New York City Council Chair Stephen and Deputy Speaker Natasha Williams hosted the New York City Convening Actions to Advance Youth Justice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: This special convening brought together young people, New York City Council members, service providers, community organizations, and system stakeholders from across the five boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Grounded in the lived experiences of youth, the discussion focused on the needs of those impacted by the juvenile and criminal legal system and explored strategies to strengthen prevention, intervention, and reentry efforts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: In May 2026, the Youth Convening Report was released.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Quick turnover.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: This report was co-produced, again, by the Deputy Speaker and the Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: the New York City Youth Justice Coalition that details findings from the convening and offer concrete recommendations for how to bring youth services to scale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Some key high-level takeaways are justice-involved youth require tailored and trauma-informed services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Girls in the justice system face unique challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Interventions must be comprehensive and holistic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Re-entry and aftercare require earlier planning and continued support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Re-Juvenile Justice and Crossroads Horizon Close to Home, on top of the fact that we need to be addressing the crisis, we ask that for increased funding for more community-based aftercare support, youth development supports, vocational career opportunities,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: GD classes, counseling, and job development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: We are also calling on the council to support the Youth Justice Innovation legislation, which would direct $50 million

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: to community-based organizations to provide a continuum of services from prevention, early intervention, to alternatives to detention, placement, and incarceration for youth age 12 through 25.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: We continue to advocate for restoration of critical prevention programs that were cut by the DOP over the past two years, such as Next Steps and Works Plus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: These smaller, hyper-local, high-touch programs allow us to give intensive levels of support to the most at-risk falling through the cracks, and they are a crucial part of the solution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: In conclusion, we urge the councils to continue to demand that the administration respond to and address the needs of children, youth, and family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: and fully support nonprofit human sector, which is the backbone of social services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: We also know that the safest communities are the fully reserved communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nikisha Francis
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: David Moss of the New York Civil Liberties Union supports Reso 274 and Intro 447 but opposes Intro 629 as written. He says ACS should not house the review teams, public defenders must be guaranteed representation, and confidentiality guardrails are needed.
chapters.title: NYCLU's David Moss supports Reso 274 and Intro 447, opposes Intro 629

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: Hi, Chair Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: Thank you to you and to the committee for this opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: My name is David Moss, and I serve as policy counsel at the New York Civil Liberties Union.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: We applaud the committee for holding this urgent hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: As you have emphasized, New York City's juvenile detention facilities, Crossroads and Horizon, are in crisis, with young people sleeping in classrooms and common areas as the two facilities flagrantly exceed their maximum capacity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: Subjecting young people to these conditions is unconscionable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: We urge the committee to approve Resolution 274 and Intro 447.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: And while we appreciate the intent of Intro 629, we do have concerns about how it would be implemented, and we do not advise the committee to move forward with the bill as it's currently written.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: With regard to Resolution 274, we note that New York City has outperformed the rest of the state in terms of raise-the-age implementation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: The city transfers more cases from criminal court to family court than the rest of the state combined, and it has outpaced the state in terms of reducing youth arrests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: The results are profound, with young people more likely to receive developmentally appropriate services that address the root causes of safety and well-being.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: And despite these facts and the fact that New York City houses half of the state's youth justice system, it is nevertheless put at a disadvantage by state funding provisions that preclude it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: from reimbursements that other jurisdictions are eligible to collect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: In a worst case but realistic scenario, this could force the city to compromise vital raise the age funding in favor of other necessary expenses or vice versa.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
utterances.text: By calling on the state legislature to eliminate this barrier, Resolution 274 is a step in the right direction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Moss
